newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Turbine has huge promise - NZ's Fletcher Energy.
newsitem.headline: Turbine has huge promise - NZ's Fletcher Energy.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Oct 21 - A new micro-turbine being developed by an associate of Fletcher Energy could be to the electricity industry what the micro-computer was to the mainframe computer industry, its backers said on Monday.

The New Zealand Press Association reported that Los Angeles-based Capstone Turbines has produced a 24 kilowatt turbine which is less than a metre long, weighs 75kg and runs on either low or high-pressure gas or petrol. A diesel version is also being developed.
Fletcher Energy last year spent about NZ$11 million acquiring a 22 percent interest in Capstone and the exclusive marketing rights for the turbine for Pacific rim countries, outside North America.
Fletcher Energy power and infrastructure chief executive Mike Smith said the company should know in the next couple of months whether the Capstone micro-turbine was commercially viable.
Marketing plans indicated that it should be extremely competitive, he said.
Smith said the turbine would bring generation choice closer to the consumer, and could be viable in a large house, school, small business or for supplying inaccessible customers in rural areas.
Interest from North American power utilities was huge, with some seeing it as a competitive weapon.

The turbine has one moving part and air bearings mean no lubrication is needed. Emissions are extremely low and, depending on the use made of the heat, the turbine's efficiency is rated between 30 percent to 80 percent.
